subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When egg white is whisked or heated, the change in the protein is best described as:
questions.explain: Heat or mechanical action unfolds (denatures) the protein, which then sets by coagulating.

questions.q: Most pathogenic bacteria grow best at a pH close to:
questions.explain: Most food-poisoning bacteria favour near-neutral pH, which is why acidity is used to preserve foods.

questions.q: The Maillard reaction responsible for the brown crust on roast meat is a reaction between:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is non-enzymic browning between amino acids and reducing sugars on heating.

questions.q: Vitamin D is important in the diet because it:
options: Promotes absorption of calcium and phosphorus
Acts as an antioxidant in cell membranes
questions.explain: Vitamin D regulates calcium and phosphorus absorption, essential for healthy bones and teeth.

questions.q: Gelatinisation occurs when:
options: Starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating, thickening the mixture
Amino acids react with reducing sugars
Sugar is heated until it browns
Fat and water are mixed with an emulsifier
questions.explain: On heating in liquid, starch granules absorb water, swell and burst, thickening the sauce.

questions.q: In HACCP, a 'critical control point' is a step at which:
options: Control is essential to prevent or eliminate a hazard
questions.explain: A critical control point is a stage where control is essential to remove or reduce a hazard to a safe level.

questions.q: Mould growth on cheese such as blue cheese is an example of:
options: A harmful pathogen always causing illness
questions.explain: Certain moulds are cultivated deliberately to ripen and flavour foods like blue cheese.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of HACCP in a food business?
options: To advertise the product to consumers
To identify and control critical points where hazards may occur
To set the retail price of food
questions.explain: HACCP systematically identifies hazards and the critical control points where they must be controlled.

questions.q: E. coli O157 is a particularly dangerous pathogen because it:
options: Is destroyed instantly at fridge temperatures
Produces a toxin that can cause severe illness and kidney damage from a low dose
questions.explain: E. coli O157 needs only a small infective dose and can cause serious illness including kidney failure.

questions.q: Gluten, important in bread structure, is formed when which two proteins combine with water?
questions.explain: Glutenin and gliadin in wheat flour combine with water to form the elastic gluten network.

questions.q: In bread-making, the biological raising of the dough is produced by:
options: Yeast fermenting sugars to release carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Yeast ferments sugars, producing carbon dioxide that makes bread dough rise.

questions.q: Cross-contamination in a kitchen is best prevented by:
options: Storing raw meat above ready-to-eat food
Using separate colour-coded boards for raw and cooked foods
Defrosting meat on a worktop overnight
Using the same knife for raw and cooked items
questions.explain: Separating raw and cooked foods, e.g. with colour-coded boards, prevents bacteria transferring between them.

questions.q: In UK Dietary Reference Values, the Reference Nutrient Intake (RNI) is the amount of a nutrient that is:
options: An average for the whole population
Enough for almost all (about 97.5%) of the population group
The minimum needed by the few with lowest needs
questions.explain: The RNI meets the needs of about 97.5% of people in a group, so most will be adequately supplied.

questions.q: For food to be certified halal, the most important requirement is that:
options: It is only ever served cold
It contains no pork and meat is slaughtered according to Islamic law
It is completely free from carbohydrate
questions.explain: Halal food excludes pork and requires permitted animals to be slaughtered according to Islamic law.

questions.q: Preservation by canning relies mainly on which principle?
options: High-temperature heat treatment to destroy micro-organisms and sealing to prevent re-contamination
Removing oxygen by modified atmosphere only
Lowering the temperature to slow bacteria
Adding acid to lower the pH
questions.explain: Canning uses heat to destroy micro-organisms and an airtight seal to keep the food sterile.

questions.q: Which group of people has an increased requirement for iron and folate?
questions.explain: Pregnancy raises iron needs for increased blood volume and folate to prevent neural tube defects.

questions.q: Which raising agent works by producing carbon dioxide when it reacts with an acid and moisture?
questions.explain: Baking powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid that release CO2 to aerate mixtures.

questions.q: Which is an example of an ethical factor influencing food choice?
options: Selecting a familiar brand by habit
Choosing free-range eggs on animal-welfare grounds
Choosing food because it is cheapest
questions.explain: Ethical choices, such as welfare-friendly or fair-trade products, are based on moral concerns.

questions.q: Which mineral is most associated with the prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; a deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Which factor would increase an adult's basal metabolic rate?
options: A greater proportion of lean muscle mass
questions.explain: Lean muscle is metabolically active, so a higher muscle mass raises BMR.

questions.q: 'Food provenance' refers to:
options: The retail price of the food
The number of calories in a food
Where and how food was grown, reared or caught
questions.explain: Provenance concerns the origin and production method of food, increasingly important to consumers.

questions.q: Bacterial spores, such as those of Clostridium and Bacillus, are a hazard because they:
options: Can survive normal cooking temperatures and germinate later
questions.explain: Heat-resistant spores can survive cooking and germinate into active bacteria if food is mishandled.

questions.q: To check that cooked food has reached a safe internal temperature, it should reach a core temperature of at least:
questions.explain: A core temperature of 75 degrees C ensures harmful bacteria in the centre of the food are destroyed.

questions.q: Which type of fatty acid contains no carbon-to-carbon double bonds?
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have all carbon bonds filled with hydrogen and no double bonds.

questions.q: Caramelisation differs from the Maillard reaction because it involves:
options: A reaction of proteins with sugars
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar alone when heated, without amino acids.

questions.q: Lecithin in egg yolk acts as an emulsifier in mayonnaise because it:
options: Has one part attracted to oil and one part attracted to water
Raises the pH of the mixture
Thickens the mixture by absorbing water
Coagulates the oil into solid particles
questions.explain: An emulsifier has hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends, holding oil and water together as a stable emulsion.

questions.q: Clostridium perfringens is often linked to food poisoning from:
options: Large quantities of meat or stews left to cool slowly
questions.explain: C. perfringens spores survive cooking and multiply when bulk-cooked meat dishes cool too slowly.

questions.q: A complete protein from a single plant source that supplies all essential amino acids is:
questions.explain: Soya is unusual among plant foods in supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Listeria monocytogenes is of special concern because, unlike most pathogens, it can:
questions.explain: Listeria can multiply slowly at fridge temperatures, posing a risk in chilled ready-to-eat foods.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is most directly linked to a long-term deficiency of:
questions.explain: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D reduce bone mineral density, leading to brittle bones.
